tool_input.description: Add Uint variant and check crate

result_text:
A JSON app config with an `env` value above `i64::MAX`, up to `u64::MAX`, now loads and is stored as its exact decimal digits. `cargo check -p shep-core` passes; I ran no tests.

**What changed** (all in `crates/shep-core/src/config/app.rs`):
1. `EnvValue` has a new `Uint(u64)` variant, next to `Int(i64)`.
2. `visit_u64` now keeps the value as `Uint(v)`. Before, it tried to convert it to `i64`, which errored above `i64::MAX`.
3. `into_string` turns `Uint` into its decimal digits, so env values are still written out as strings.

Negative numbers down to `i64::MIN`, strings, booleans and floats go through the same code as before.

**TOML is different.** The TOML format only allows signed 64-bit integers, so the `toml` parser most likely rejects a number above `i64::MAX` before this code sees it. A change in this file can't fix that. The fix works for JSON configs; in a Flockfile, a number that large still has to be written as a quoted string.

Next: run `cargo test -p shep-core --lib` to confirm the existing env tests still pass.
